successors.note: 'Wei took over all of Gongsun Yuan's territories, including Lelang and Daifang' (Goguryeo-Wei War page); 'Liaodong and present-day northwest Korea became Wei territories' (Gongsun Yuan page).

capitals.note: The Gongsun Yuan page names Xiangping only as the place Sima Yi besieged in 238 and never calls it a capital; the Gongsun Kang page has Kang as Marquis of Xiangping.

The Du page says only that he 'took over Liaoning' and was Administrator of Liaodong from 190; the Four Commanderies page calls him 'Liaodong administrator in 189'. No area on either page.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Kang 'controlled the territories of Liaodong, Xuantu and Lelang commanderies' in 204 and cut Daifang from Lelang; Yuan lost 'Liaodong, Lelang and Daifang' to Wei in 238. Cliopatria's Cao Cao shape (207..223, bbox to 127E, 42N) and Cao Wei shape (224..264) draw all of this as Cao land, so the Cliopatria cover for these years is wrong inside the Gongsun territory; the renderer should let this state win from 204. No area on the pages.

region.text: Liaodong Commandery, Gongsun Du's base (the Du page: he 'took over Liaoning')

ledger.note: 190: Gongsun Du takes Liaodong. Gongsun Du page infobox: Administrator of Liaodong 'In office 190-204' and Governor of Ping Province (self-appointed, dates unknown); Four Commanderies page: 'Gongsun Du became Liaodong administrator in 189'. He 'took over Liaoning' and, undated, 'took control of the existing Daifang and Lelang commanderies' (the page's wording; Daifang did not yet exist).

region.text: Lelang and Xuantu as Kang's inheritance

ledger.note: 204: Gongsun Kang inherits Liaodong, Xuantu and Lelang. 'In 204, he inherited his father's appointment and controlled the territories of Liaodong, Xuantu and Lelang commanderies.' The page gives the year Kang held them, not the year Du took them: Du's Lelang and Xuantu acquisition is undated. Same year Daifang is cut from Lelang (Four Commanderies page).

region.text: 'some of [Goguryeo's] territory' seized in Kang's second campaign; the page names no place, the Goguryeo-Xuantu frontier is a placeholder

ledger.note: 209: Kang's second invasion of Goguryeo. 'Kang invaded Goguryeo again in 209 and seized some of its territory and weakened Goguryeo.' In 204 he had 'helped invade Goguryeo after the older brother of King Sansang, Balgi'. The land is not named; confidence 1.
209: the campaign ends with Goguryeo weakened; no later fighting is on the page.
237: Gongsun Yuan proclaims the state of Yan. 'He rebelled against Wei in 237 and declared himself "King of Yan" (燕王).' Colour and dossier continue.

region.text: Liaodong Commandery, Gongsun Du's base (the Du page: he 'took over Liaoning')

ledger.note: 238: Sima Yi marches on Liaodong. 'In 238, the Cao Wei general Sima Yi led forces to Liaodong and successfully conquered Yan.' The Goguryeo-Wei War page has Goguryeo allied with Wei in the same campaign and Xi'anping, at the Yalu mouth, 'overrun by Wei in 238'. The month of the start is not on the page.

ledger.note: September 238: Xiangping falls. The Gongsun Yuan footnotes give the siege 'on the bingyin day of the 8th month' (3 September in the page's conversion) and the fall on the renwu day (19 September); Yuan dies c. September 238.

ledger.note: 238: the Gongsun state ends with Yuan's death. Reign 237 to c. September 238 (infobox); the page is silent on any Gongsun remnant.

wars.name: Gongsun Kang's wars on Goguryeo
wars.outcome: Kang helped Balgi invade Goguryeo in 204 and invaded again in 209, seizing some territory.
wars.note: Goguryeo's own account (Taejo, Sansang pages) was not opened.

wars.name: Sima Yi's conquest of Yan

zones.text: Liaodong Commandery, Gongsun Du's base (the Du page: he 'took over Liaoning')

wars.outcome: Sima Yi besieges Xiangping from the 8th month and takes it; Gongsun Yuan dies; Wei annexes Liaodong, Lelang and Daifang; Goguryeo allied with Wei.
wars.note: Sources differ on the day (3 September siege, 19 September fall in the page's footnotes).

certainty.note: The pages name commanderies, not boundaries; the Xuantu and Lelang extents are those of the commandery dossiers.

notes: State that Cliopatria lacks: the Gongsun warlords of Liaodong (190-238), whose land Cliopatria folds into Cao Cao (207..223) and Cao Wei (224..264). Rulers are not given as a strip because the pages disagree: the Du page has him in office 190-204, the Kang page infobox puts Kang's office at 204-210 and his death in 210 while its footnote has him dying 'between 209 and Dec 220', Gong's term is undated, Yuan seizes power in 228 'from his uncle Gongsun Gong' and reigns 237 to c. September 238 as King of Yan. The dealings with Wu (the Wu envoys killed in late 233) are not territorial. No Wikipedia article for the regime as such was opened (the title in `wikipedia` is the founder's). The Yuan brothers fled to Kang in c. December 207 and Kang sent their heads to Cao Cao (Kang page).
